claims.text: The solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
Removing Co increases local lattice distortions in FeNiCrMn relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Removing Co modifies short-range order in FeNiCrMn.
The altered local bonding environment raises the activation barrier for dislocation nucleation.
Co removal makes the dislocation-nucleation barrier more sensitive to temperature and strain rate.
The altered local bonding environment elevates the barrier for dislocation motion.
The lattice-distortion and short-range-order changes promote dynamic strain aging at intermediate temperatures and high strain rates.
The proposed barrier and dynamic-strain-aging effects delay dislocation nucleation.
The proposed effects delay dislocation propagation.
Under identical simulated loading, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have higher flow stress than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Under identical simulated loading, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have a higher onset strain for dislocation activity than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Co-free FeNiCrMn will preserve ductility while its flow stress is enhanced relative to the Co-containing baseline.
The predicted flow-stress and dislocation-onset differences will be strongest at intermediate temperatures and high strain rates.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the alloy remains within its solid-solution phase-stability regime.
Secondary-phase formation or significant ordering may invalidate the proposed mechanism.
